current_answer: Start with the smallest sufficient layer and keep human approval separate from execution. For a small list, first distinguish a DOI request, one immediate post-confirmation welcome, an ongoing welcome campaign, and a delayed sequence. Keep an existing operated sender only if consent, approved copy, current suppression, one accountable attempt and provider outcomes can be reconciled. Otherwise stop and repair it. For a new one-message system, privately evaluate phpList v3.6.16 if its operating burden fits, or Keila v0.30.3 for a form-centered path. Listmonk v6.2.0 needs a reviewed external/manual trigger and ledger. These are source-only choices, not send-ready or additions to the vetted four-layer shortlist. If a Ghost publication site is already operated, its native one-message member welcome is a conditional alternative to another list stack, subject to the same installed-build, consent, approval, suppression, provider-outcome and recovery evidence. Do not install Ghost solely for a small-list welcome by default; its optional timed sequences are a separate beta evaluation. Ghost is not send-vetted or a four-layer shortlist addition. For social-post client review, Postiz v2.25.0 offers documented draft preview comments but no enforced approval flag. A connected channel is prerequisite in the documented composer/API paths, so a no-channel draft must not be promised. Keep sign-off in a separate auditable record and limit scheduling access; do not add Postiz to the vetted shortlist or treat this source audit as a live/provider/security test. For newsletter measurement, self-hosted Umami v3.4.0 can count UTM-tagged site page views and a separately instrumented signup signal, then present a goal rate and first-/last-click attribution. This is a source-only post-click measurement option; it does not verify newsletter delivery, a created account, revenue or causal ROI. Use a private synthetic pilot and reconcile events with the authoritative account system. Umami is not a four-layer shortlist addition.

catalogue_card.question: Which open-source marketing projects, AI agents and harnesses are worth using, and for which tasks?
catalogue_card.text: A source-linked catalogue with conditional choices, explicit license and execution boundaries, and a draft-only first-test rule.

summary: Mautic and Activepieces CE are conditional choices for teams able to operate their platform or workflow layer.
n8n is a source-available/fair-code workflow and optional AI orchestration option; its Sustainable Use License is not OSI-style open source and may restrict commercial provision/hosting.
Marketing Agent OS is a portable harness library, not a marketing application. Its 25 September audit found a component-level provenance boundary and host-owned execution controls.
Loopmark is retained only under the direct label ‘exploratory local drafting CLI’. MarketingOS AI was examined but is not recommended or catalogued.
The research library contains dated dossiers and permanent report links for all completed research runs.
The 24 September operations guide distinguishes a local Mautic form/contact artifact from a local Activepieces CE run artifact and requires human review and teardown for either.

The 26 September Mautic 7.2.1 audit documents campaign, preference, queue, cron, role, and report surfaces while separating them from operator-owned consent, delivery, approval, monitoring, and recovery work.

The 27 September Activepieces CE audit documents the manual/local draft path, paid governance boundary, in-flight retry risk, encryption-key and multi-store recovery duties, and conflicting retention/log-cap documentation.
The 28 September synthesis assigns draft, exact-version human decision, optional CE run, sender/CRM action evidence, consent and recovery to distinct owners; no combined integration was tested.

The 29 September small-list audit keeps an existing operated sender as the first conditional option, Keila as a private-evaluation candidate only, and Listmonk as a list/campaign tool without an established built-in welcome trigger. Neither is added to the vetted four-layer shortlist.

The 30 September Keila v0.30.3 source follow-up read tagged README/build files and a registry digest listing. K1 partly advanced but remains open; K3 and X1 remain open. No image inspection, restore or send occurred, and no shortlist addition was made.

The 1 October Listmonk v6.2.0 tagged-path audit found no distinct native welcome in inspected DOI confirmation, core hook, template, campaign and transactional paths. A reviewed external trigger/ledger or manual action is required; /api/tx does not enforce consent or dedupe. No runtime test or shortlist addition.

The 2 October Listmonk v6.2.0 private DOI/suppression test did not run: pinned artifact, isolated runtime, local-only mail sink, egress proof and teardown were unavailable. A reproducible fictional-data test card was prepared; no observed behavior, send clearance or shortlist addition follows.

The 3 October phpList v3.6.16 audit found a tagged call to sendMail for one immediate page-keyed system confirmation message after DOI, not a delayed welcome sequence. Current docs describe editable global/page copy; exact-tag signup/editor fallback, suppression, duplicate and provider outcome remain untested. Conditional research entry only.

The 4 October small-list welcome decision contract separates DOI request, immediate welcome, ongoing campaign and delayed sequence. It puts the existing-sender evidence test first and maps consent, approval, suppression, attempt, provider outcome, duplicate hold and restore. No runtime, sink, provider or restore test occurred; no send clearance.

The 5 October Ghost v6.63.0 source audit found native member-signup welcome triggers and current help for free/paid welcome emails. Reuse is conditional on an already-operated publication site and a complete consent-to-recovery record; no install, send, provider or restore test occurred. Delayed sequences are an opt-in beta, not covered by the one-message finding.

The 6 October Marketing Agent OS one-skill installation test did not run. The intended pinned checkout was unreachable and a network-denied boundary could not be established. No skill or target was selected, no installer was executed, and no file effects were observed. No recommendation change.

The 7 October Postiz v2.25.0 audit separates unlisted preview comments from enforced client sign-off. Current docs explicitly disclaim a blocking approved flag; no-channel draft was not established. No instance, connection, provider action or security test occurred; Postiz is not shortlisted.

The 8 October Umami v3.4.0 tagged-source audit supports a synthetic post-click pilot: UTM-tagged page-view counts and a separate signup-confirmed signal. No site, newsletter, instance, goal report or browser fixture was tested; no verified account, ROI or shortlist claim.
uncertainty: No Mautic or Activepieces CE hands-on installation, configuration, form submission, delivery, flow run, integration, or security test occurred; the controlled pilots are draft plans.
No Loopmark or MarketingOS AI hands-on install or test occurred.
Loopmark’s package/release provenance and operating/security documentation remain unresolved in the checked primary material; missing documentation is not proof a capability is absent.
License labels are component-scoped taxonomy, not legal advice or a decision on a particular deployment.
Individual connectors, permissions, costs, data paths, retry routes, and approval controls require separate verification.

Marketing Agent OS provenance was not verified file-by-file against its four upstream pins; installer collision/rollback behavior, helper effects, connector scopes, release artifacts, CI outputs, and host discovery remain unverified.

The Mautic audit was documentation and repository reading only. It did not install or operate Mautic, test delivery or suppression, or establish runtime compatibility, approval controls, secret management, connector behavior, performance, backup/restore, or production readiness.

Activepieces 0.92.0 tagged license files and exact CE UI were not verified; current unversioned Limits and Truncated Logs pages conflict, and no deployed retention, flow, retry, backup, restore, alert or deletion behavior was tested.

The 28 September cross-layer handoff is synthesis of earlier dated audits only. No new source verification, integration, external action, pilot or restore occurred. The combined route is not a recommendation.

Keila v0.30.3 exact-tag licence and extra path scope were not readable; complete tested restore, current private security disclosure route, provider-event reconciliation and real send outcomes were not established. Listmonk native form/confirmation-to-welcome trigger was not established. No installation, public form, actual contact, mail send, or restore test occurred.

The v0.30.3 tagged LICENSE.md and extra/README.md, complete archive and final image were unread. The registry digest was listed, not independently checked. No coordinated DB/upload/secret restore, rollback, private security route, plain-SMTP outcome reconciliation or exactly-once behavior was verified.

The Listmonk v6.2.0 finding is bounded to inspected tagged paths, not every customization. No install or provider receipt was obtained; read/send races, concurrent workers, ambiguous responses, provider reconciliation and exactly-once welcome outcome remain unresolved. Local git/API/raw reads partly failed and were not used as absence evidence.

The Listmonk v6.2.0 confirmation/suppression matrix, read-only candidate selector, external attempt ledger, and controlled unsubscribe/confirm race remain untested. No installed-artifact digest, private app/database, local mail sink, egress proof or teardown was available on 2 October; /api/tx was not called.

phpList v3.6.16 was not installed or used to submit a form or send mail. Tagged signup library and page editor/config fallback were not fetched; current docs do not prove exact-tag behavior. No package hash, runtime, sink, provider receipt, race, rejection or restore test was obtained. The confirmation handler clears the blacklist flag and uses an earlier confirmed read; exactly-once, safe suppression, secure downloads and delivery are not established.

The 4 October decision is documentation/source synthesis, not an observed ranking. phpList exact-tag signup/editor, package, suppression and provider outcome; Keila licence/image, restore and SMTP outcomes; Listmonk supported trigger/idempotency or audited external ledger; and existing-sender records remain unverified. No product is send-ready.

Ghost v6.63.0 exact-tag signup/confirmation path, welcome/beta send adapter, duplicate claim, just-in-time suppression, provider result and automation-run restore were not verified. Current welcome and beta help are living documentation, not exact-tag proof. No package bytes, site, mail fixture, send or restore were checked; no send-ready or shortlist claim follows.

Marketing Agent OS one-skill dry-run, install, copied-file scope, hashes, file modes, repeat/collision behavior and teardown remain unobserved; the 6 October attempt stopped at pinned-checkout and network-isolation gates.

Postiz v2.25.0 tagged authorization/controller and provider code were not traced. Living documentation, not runtime tests, supports workflow, roles, token storage and failure claims. No-channel in-app draft, preview expiry/access logs, exact permission matrix, delivery, retry and credential lifecycle remain open.

Umami v3.4.0 tracker/collector/query and current docs were read, not run. Sender delivery, consent gating, redirects, blockers, duplicate/missed signup events, installed-build security, goals, attribution, data scrubbing and reconciliation with account records remain untested. The replay-advisory mitigation is a source-level observation only.
freshness_note: 8 October 2026 Umami v3.4.0 source/documentation audit: post-click measurement pilot only; no runtime, verified signup, ROI or shortlist addition.
